proposal:
STATUS. Hand-derived and unexecuted; nothing was run. This extends a preprocessor and its certificate. It is not polynomial SAT, gives no universal growth bound, and leaves residual solver work unbounded. The watcher handoff carries no statements or proofs and contributes nothing.

CERTIFICATE (00057, T_K form). M (r x n), R (n x r); per exact-support block K: local rows M_K with local right inverse R_K, a matrix T_K with M_K=T_K M, and a duplicate-free Q_K. Checks: MR=I; M_K R_K=I; M_K p in Q_K for every p in P_K; m_K=|Q_K|*2^(c_K-d_K). Fibre counting makes P_K the exact preimage of Q_K, so F(x)=G(Mx) and G(y)=F(Ry), where block K of G forbids T_K y in Q_K. No 2^n, 2^r or 2^c table. Let e_K be the number of columns T_K touches. The quotient block has |Q_K|*2^(e_K-d_K) points, a blow-up of exactly 2^(e_K-c_K) over m_K, and e_K>=d_K.

NEW MECHANISM: ATOM-REFINE. It decides exactly whether a frame with e_K=d_K for all K exists, i.e. an adapted basis of V=sum A_K. For an index set S let A_S be the intersection of the A_i, with A_empty=V. Add spaces one at a time, keeping the types S with q_S>0. Candidates at step i+1 are t and t+{i+1} for kept t. For each candidate compute A_S by one intersection, N_S=sum of A_S' over candidates S' strictly containing S, and q_S=dim A_S-dim N_S. Reject unless the q_S sum to dim V. At the end lift a basis of each A_S/N_S, take the union C, and verify that each A_i is spanned by members of C lying in A_i.

Theorem ATOM (hand proof, any field): an adapted basis exists iff ATOM-REFINE accepts. Sketch: let B be adapted and type(b)={i: b in A_i}. Then A_S=span{b: type(b) contains S}, and the sum of A_T over T strictly above S is span{b: type(b) strictly contains S}. Hence q_S counts basis vectors of type S, the counts sum to dim V, candidate sums equal full sums, and kept types are the true restricted types. Downward induction on S shows arbitrary lifts span every A_S; cardinality makes C a basis. The converse is the final verification. Rejection is therefore a proof of non-existence for these spaces, not a greedy artefact. There are at most 2*dim V candidates per step.

BIT-WORK, separately (crude hand bounds; L=encoded length, c=max width, m blocks).
- Grouping: O(L log L).
- Stabilisers: only p0+p with p in P_K can stabilise, so the total is sum m_K^2 c_K <= L^2.
- Annihilators: sum c_K^3.
- ATOM-REFINE: O(m n^5).
- Right inverse: Gauss-Jordan pivots, R=pivot embedding times inverse pivot minor, O(r^2 n).
- Checks: O(r^2 n + m c r n + L c).
- Coefficients: every entry is one bit; the only integers are m_K and |Q_K|, at most c_K+1 bits; no rationals or HNF.
- Certificate: O(n^2 + m c n + L) bits.
- Quotient when e_K=d_K: r<n; clause count and widths do not increase.
- Width: unbounded, since m_K>=2^(c_K-d_K) is already paid by the input.
- Residual work on G: NOT bounded.

WHERE FR-KAPPA HELPS.
(i) Local relaxation is free: the checks accept any K-local rows whose span contains A_K. Example W: parity blocks x1+x2=1, x3+x4=1, x1+x2+x3+x4=0 (12 clauses). The exact spaces are three dependent lines, so ATOM-REFINE rejects. Replacing A_K by V intersect Forms(K) gives block 3 the space span(x1+x2,x3+x4), r=2, and the count check reads 8=2*4.
(ii) That relaxation is not monotone. The frame {x1,x2+x3,x3+x4} serves a block on {1,2,4} with space span(x1), but saturation adds x2+x4 and breaks it.
(iii) Non-local frames can beat every frame built from block forms; see N_t.
(iv) It never helps blocks with trivial stabiliser, which includes all odd-sized blocks. There A_K=Forms(K), and if these cover all variables then r=n.

ADVERSARIES (described, not run).
D_t, n=2t: u_i=x_(2i-1)+x_(2i); block i on variables 2i-1..2i+2 forbids the four points with u_i=u_(i+1)=1; 4(t-1) clauses. Prediction for t=8,12,16: exactly t types, each q=1; r=t; G is t-1 binary clauses; SAT; zero assignment enumeration.

N_t, n=t=3q, indices mod t: parity blocks a_i=x_i+x_(i+1)+x_(i+2)=b_i, 4t clauses. Hand-derived:
- The rank is t-2, because 1+z+z^2 divides z^t+1, so no adapted basis exists.
- V intersect Forms(K_i)=span(a_i), so local relaxation also rejects.
- Every relation has weight 2q, so any frame chosen among the a_i has e_K=2q-1 for both dropped blocks, a blow-up of 2^(2q-4).
- The telescoped frame beta_j=a_(j+3)+a_(j+6)+... (j=0..t-4) with beta_*=x_0+...+x_(t-1) gives a_i=beta_i+beta_(i-3). For i<=2, beta_* replaces the missing term; for i>=t-3 there is one term only. So e_K<=2, r=t-2, and G is 2-CNF with 2t-3 clauses.
Predictions for t=18,24,30: ATOM-REFINE rejects with count t against t-2, and the telescoped certificate passes all checks. Pinned v2 at t=12 (48 clauses) must skip compression if it uses exact annihilator spaces; I do not predict its peak.

LABELS. Log COMPRESSED / INCOMPATIBLE (count mismatch) / NO-STABILISER separately from solver peak. The extra-clause controls are NO-STABILISER with peaks 0 and 9, so compression failure and trace hardness are different axes.
missing_theorem:
T94 (first; Lean, general n, no sorry). The four checks imply F(x)=G(Mx) and G(y)=F(Ry), including the T_K form. The proof should be compositional: (a) fibre counting for a GF(2) map with explicit right inverse, (b) support restriction, (c) list induction over blocks. Instances then check only the certificate, row by row. This is still not machine-checked; CompressionSoundness.lean covers complete enumeration only.

T97 (Lean, any field). Theorem ATOM in both directions, plus the candidate-sum lemma. It is a hand proof only. If it survives checking, it settles the adapted-basis half of 00057's T95.

T98 (open; the exact theorem for incompatible spaces). SPARSE-FRAME(kappa): given supports K_i and spaces A_i inside Forms(K_i), decide whether there is an independent set B of fewer than n forms, spanning all A_i, with e_i <= c_i+kappa for every i. Either give a polynomial algorithm or prove NP-hardness. ATOM-REFINE solves only the case e_i=d_i for the exact spaces and for the saturated spaces. The telescoped frame for N_t was found by hand from cyclic structure. I recall that sparsest null-space-basis problems are NP-hard, but that is from memory and is not the same problem. I have no reduction and no algorithm.

T96 (arbitrary extra clauses, unchanged). By the 00057 padding lemma (hand proof), deciding G(Mx) and H(x) for arbitrary H is NP-complete. An unconditional extra-clause theorem is therefore polynomial SAT itself. Only conditional versions are provable targets, and none is proved.
self_attack:
1. ATOM is short linear algebra and unchecked. In the rejecting case the intermediate numbers mean nothing beyond rejection, because candidate sums equal full sums only when an adapted basis exists.
2. Completeness is for a FIXED family of spaces. Example W and N_t show the exact family can fail while a relaxed or non-local frame succeeds. INCOMPATIBLE therefore does not mean incompressible, and that gap is exactly T98.
3. While drafting I first believed every frame for N_t needs e about 2q. That is false: it holds only for frames drawn from the block forms. Lower bounds on e_K for general frames are unproved everywhere.
4. Nothing here touches hardness. D_t reduces to 2-SAT and N_t is a linear system. They test certificates and labels, not the solver. No growth bound follows.
5. Exact-support grouping misses cross-support subsumption and compressions visible only after resolution.
6. O(m n^5) is crude and gives no n^2 or n^3 claim.
7. The v2 skip predictions for N_12 and W assume v2 uses exact annihilator spaces only; I have not seen the code. auto00008 stays unclassified until ATOM-REFINE is actually run on it.
8. Extra clauses: no progress. Odd-block controls defeat every stabiliser-based method here.
9. Kernel decide at n=32 within 45 seconds is untested.

delta_from_prior:
00057 gave the LQC certificate and left adapted-basis discovery (T95) open, with an unchecked lattice recollection.

New here:
(1) ATOM-REFINE with an elementary two-direction hand proof. It turns a greedy skip into an exact accept/reject for a fixed family and no longer needs the lattice criterion.
(2) The exact FR-kappa blow-up 2^(e_K-c_K), and the observation that K-local relaxation is free under the existing checks (example W). Saturation is shown not to be monotone.
(3) Family N_t: no adapted basis exists, frames built from block forms cost 2^(2q-4), and a hand-built non-local frame gives e_K<=2. This separates block-form discovery from general frames.
(4) SPARSE-FRAME as the precise open problem for incompatible spaces.
(5) Family D_t and three-way logging.

Not new: LQC soundness, the padding lemma and T94. There is no result on extra clauses, nonlinear gadgets, auto00008, auto00009 or any universal bound.
